chunks.text: 72-year-old male, Retired, resident of Ang Mo Kio, Singapore.
Fractured left radius (20 years ago, healed)
Discontinued Enalapril due to cough (2 years ago)
General anesthesia with spinal anesthesia as adjunct for intraoperative pain control

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good morning, Mr. Tan. I'm Dr. Liew, the anesthesiologist who'll be taking care of you during your hip replacement surgery. Can you tell me a bit about why you're having this surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Morning, doctor. My right hip been hurting a lot, especially when walking. X-ray show severe arthritis, so doctor say need to replace it lah.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you. Let's go through your medications. I see you're on quite a few – can you confirm what you're currently taking?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Sure. I take Amlodipine 5mg every day for blood pressure, Metformin 500mg twice daily for diabetes, Insulin glargine 20 units at night. Furosemide 20mg only when I have swelling, Tamsulosin for prostate, Aspirin 75mg daily, Pantoprazole 40mg daily, and Atorvastatin 20mg nightly.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Have there been any changes to your medications in the last year, particularly with your acid suppression medication?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Oh yes! I stopped Ranitidine about six months ago because of that big recall news. My GP switched me to Pantoprazole 40mg daily since then.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thanks for clarifying that. Are all your other medications still the same doses as listed?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, doctor. Everything else same as before. Only the Ranitidine changed to Pantoprazole.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good to know. Any allergies we should know about?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I get a rash from Penicillin. That's the only one.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Noted. Have you had any previous anesthesia or surgeries?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Had a spinal block for my cataract surgery last year. No problems at all, very smooth.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Excellent. What about your fasting status today?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I had a light breakfast around 6am, nothing since 8am. Just some water for meds lah.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Perfect. Finally, how's your mobility before surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Can walk with a cane, but pain makes it difficult. Need help with stairs sometimes.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for all that information, Mr. Tan. We'll be using general anesthesia with spinal anesthesia for pain control during surgery. Any questions for me?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No questions, doctor. Just want to get this done and walk properly again.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:00] induction propofol one hundred twenty milligrams, fentanyl forty micrograms

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:02] tube in, grade one view

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:05] right radial artery line placed

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:10] five hundred milliliters normal saline bolus

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:15] mean arterial pressure dropped to fifty-five, treated with phenylephrine one hundred micrograms

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Hi there, how are you feeling now after the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Got some pain at the hip, but the meds help. Feeling a bit dizzy and nauseous though.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Okay, we can give you something for the nausea. Any trouble breathing or sore throat?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Throat's a bit sore, but breathing's fine.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That's from the tube during anesthesia. Do you remember anything from the operation?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Not really, I was out cold.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That's normal. Now, regarding your other conditions – how's your blood pressure, sugar levels, and kidneys?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: All seem okay. No issues so far.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. Any discomfort from BPH or need to urinate?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Not really, but I'm a bit thirsty.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: We'll monitor your fluids and check your blood sugar and BP regularly. Rest well.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Thanks, doctor.

72-year-old male undergoing elective total hip replacement surgery under general anesthesia with spinal anesthesia as adjunct for intraoperative pain control. Intraoperative course includes induction with propofol, successful intubation, arterial line placement, fluid bolus administration, and transient hypotension treated with phenylephrine.

Patient has a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, chronic kidney disease stage 2, osteoarthritis (right hip), and benign prostatic hyperplasia. He uses pantoprazole 40 mg daily, suggesting possible GERD. Current medications include amlodipine, metformin, insulin glargine, furosemide PRN, tamsulosin, aspirin, pantoprazole, and atorvastatin. He has a penicillin allergy (rash) and is ASA-PS Class III. Last meal at 6:00 AM, NPO since 8:00 AM except water for medications.

Anticipated postoperative challenges include PONV risk due to GERD and opioid use, hemodynamic instability from chronic hypertension and intraoperative hypotension, glycemic control difficulties due to diabetes and metformin continuation, urinary retention risk from BPH and spinal anesthesia, bleeding risk from aspirin continuation and major surgery, renal function monitoring needs due to CKD, fluid bolus, and hypotension, aspiration risk from GERD and general anesthesia, and analgesia requirements for major orthopedic surgery with spinal adjunct.

Evaluate aspirin continuation perioperatively with cardiac risk assessment. Monitor for postoperative nausea and vomiting, considering antiemetic prophylaxis. Maintain close blood pressure monitoring and be prepared for vasopressor support if needed. Closely monitor glucose levels and adjust insulin accordingly. Assess for urinary retention postoperatively. Monitor for surgical site bleeding and ensure hemostasis. Check renal function (serum creatinine, eGFR, urine output) postoperatively. Ensure NPO status and consider continuation of pantoprazole for aspiration risk mitigation. Manage analgesia with spinal anesthesia adjunct and supplemental medications as needed. Hold metformin postoperatively and monitor for signs of lactic acidosis.
